solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gushing from breast of young female thespian Titan accepting Oscar

indicators.note: accepting means the Titan's name takes the next letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a thespian is a stage performer
Rhea is a Titaness of Greek myth, mother of Zeus
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A young actress playing a Titan, apparently with an Oscar in hand, is described in some gushing moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young female' wants to be part of the definition, but the definition stops at 'breast'. Rhea is a Titaness in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactorrhoea is the medical term for spontaneous flow of milk from the nipple outside normal nursing.

clue.text: Early bloomer's brilliance involving bent for honesty

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the word for brilliance encloses the rest

parts.note: a glow is a radiant brightness

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the following words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A flower praised for its early brilliance and some leaning toward honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent for honesty' reads as an inclination, but bent is the shuffle signal and 'for' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory-of-the-snow (Chionodoxa) is a small blue spring bulb that flowers as the snow melts, hence an early bloomer.

clue.text: Detection system needs days to break someone dishonest

indicators.note: to break into a word means to burst inside it, so the days letter goes into the middle

parts.note: a liar is a person who is not honest
d is the standard abbreviation for day or days

explanation.surface: A lie detector must take days to crack someone who is lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Lidar is a laser-based ranging technique, like radar using light, that detects and measures distant objects.

clue.text: Monkey and Swan getting central makeover with broken loom installed

indicators.note: installed means put in place inside, so the jumbled loom goes into the middle of the Swan
a makeover at the centre means the middle two letters of the constellation's name are rearranged

parts.note: Cygnus, Latin for swan, is the Swan constellation

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, so the letters of loom are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A monkey and a swan get makeovers while a broken loom is fitted somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan is capitalised because it names the constellation; only its two middle letters swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynomolgus is the crab-eating macaque, a long-tailed Asian monkey widely used in research.

clue.text: Founders of early punk rock band with provocative image — time to split

parts.note: Oi! was a street-punk style of the late 1970s

indicators.note: to split something is to come between its parts, so the time letter goes inside the band's name

parts.note: Kiss are the face-painted American rock band known for outrageous shows
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A music-history line about who founded early punk and which shock-rock band split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founders of early punk' wants to be the definition, but 'of' is a link and early punk is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An oikist was the leader who founded an ancient Greek colony, so oikists are colony founders.

clue.text: Gold standard precedes hoarding old stack of coins

indicators.note: precedes says the standard part comes before the gold part in the answer
hoarding means keeping stored away inside, so the standard holds the old letter

parts.note: a rule is a standard or norm
o is the abbreviation for old
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A note on the gold standard and old hoards of coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold standard' looks like one phrase, but the gold comes last: RULE holding O, then AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouleau is a cylindrical roll of coins wrapped in paper, a stack laid on its side.

clue.text: Durban nanny's phrase giving permission to leave unknown things behind

indicators.note: to leave things is to drop them, so those letters are removed from the phrase
behind completes 'leave behind', abandoning them rather than keeping them in the phrase

parts.note: 'you may' is what someone says to allow something
y is a standard algebraic unknown; two unknowns are two of them

explanation.surface: A South African nanny says something allowing a child to go, leaving unknown things behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ys go from YOU MAY. 'Nanny' here is the British pet word for grandmother, not a hired carer, and Durban places it in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouma is the Afrikaans and South African English word for grandmother, the equivalent of a granny.

clue.text: Involving death of cells, each accompanied by involuntary action

parts.note: 'a pop' means each, as in five pounds a pop
to can mean with musical accompaniment, as in dancing to a band
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding note on cell death, each case accompanied by a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoptosis is programmed cell death, and the adjective apoptotic describes processes relating to it.

clue.text: Split into regions dividing refined petrol, see their damage is stratospheric

indicators.note: dividing means splitting something apart by sitting inside it
refined petrol is processed, so these letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
an area split into regions has been zoned

explanation.surface: Refined petrol and zoned regions sit beside a warning about high-altitude damage.
explanation.walkthrough: ZONED sits after the first letter of the rearranged PETROL SEE. 'Stratospheric' is both literal (the ozone layer is in the stratosphere) and slang for enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone-depleting chemicals such as CFCs thin the protective ozone layer high in the stratosphere.

clue.text: British pianist seeing Beck turn back

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the words are read from the end

parts.note: a beck is a gesture of the head, as in beck and call; a nod
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A British pianist watches the musician Beck turn around.
explanation.walkthrough: Beck looks like the American musician but is a nod, the beckoning motion behind 'beck and call'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ogdon was an English concert pianist who jointly won the 1962 Tchaikovsky Competition.

clue.text: Elfin forest spirit maiden in Tolkien's Middle Earth ultimately left in fantasy land

indicators.note: middle points to the central letter of the author's name

parts.note: the central letter of the seven-letter name
rum is a spirit drink
m is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the planet's name is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: in places the spirit and maiden inside the letters taken from the author and Earth

parts.note: Oz is the magical land of the Wizard of Oz
l is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A spirit maiden of Tolkien's Middle Earth is finally left in a fantasy land, an elfin forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle Earth' reads as Tolkien's world but splits: 'Tolkien's Middle' and 'Earth ultimately' each give one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Krummholz is stunted, wind-twisted tree growth at the treeline, also called elfin wood or elfin forest.

clue.text: US boss of transport arrangements could make trams ready

indicators.note: arrangements are settings in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An American transport chief's arrangements might get the trams ready to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport arrangements' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'transport'.
explanation.definitionFit: In American railroading a yardmaster supervises a rail yard, directing the switching and makeup of trains.

clue.text: Obsessive admirer ignoring the archenemy's earlier article

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Satan is the arch-enemy of God and mankind
a is the indefinite article; the earlier of the two is dropped

explanation.surface: An obsessive fan pays no attention to the villain's earlier article.
explanation.walkthrough: SATAN has two As; only the first goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan is slang, from the Eminem song, for an overzealous or obsessive fan of a celebrity.

clue.text: A medical scan covering small screen, see you living forever!

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the farewell surrounds the screen letters

parts.note: taken as written
MRI is magnetic resonance imaging
ta-ta is a casual goodbye
the small screen is a nickname for television

explanation.surface: A medical scan of a TV screen ends with a cheery farewell and a wish for eternal life.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to 'see you', which is a goodbye rather than a verb of seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritattva is the Sanskrit term for immortality, the state of being deathless or eternal.

clue.text: Liberal in Edinburgh college knocks the rough edges off

indicators.note: in places the party letter inside the school's name

parts.note: Fettes College is a well-known private school in Edinburgh
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal at an Edinburgh school smooths the rough edges off things.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside FETTES, which is a boarding school, not a university.
explanation.definitionFit: To fettle is to trim and smooth a casting or pot, removing the burrs and rough seams.

clue.text: Yellow-flowered plant that stings wife in the chest

indicators.note: in places the cry and the wife letter inside the body part

parts.note: the thorax is the chest cavity
ow is a cry of pain, what one says when something stings
w is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A yellow plant that stings stings someone's wife in the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That stings' looks like a description of the plant, but it is a cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorow-wax is a Eurasian umbellifer, Bupleurum rotundifolium, bearing small greenish-yellow flowers.

clue.text: Returning prisoner has months inside, not having been assessed

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
inside places the months letter within the prisoner word

parts.note: a détenu is a person held in custody, especially a political prisoner
m is the abbreviation for month or months

explanation.surface: A prisoner comes back after months inside, his case never assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Months inside' sounds like a prison term, but it is a single M placed within the prisoner word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete is to measure or allot, so something unmeted has not been measured out or judged.

clue.text: Turn of Britain to get into American basketball? They don't plan to do it

definitions.text: They don't plan to do it

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it

parts.note: hoops is American slang for basketball

indicators.note: a turn of the country's code turns it round to face the other way

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A question of whether Britain is turning to American basketball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do it' is a euphemism for sex, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook-up is a casual, unplanned sexual encounter, so the people involved never set out intending one.

clue.text: Second, third and fourth Mrs Barlow losing a daughter turned up close together

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top
losing means going without, so one letter drops out of the name

parts.note: Deirdre married Ken Barlow of Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap, twice, as his third and fourth wife
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A soap trivia line: Ken Barlow's second, third and fourth wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second, third and fourth' reads as a list, but Second is S and 'third and fourth Mrs Barlow' is Deirdre. Dropping one D gives DEIRRE, turned up as ERRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Serried describes ranks or rows pressed closely together, as of troops standing shoulder to shoulder.

clue.text: Shooter of archduke and king included in hit with bullet

indicators.note: in places the king and the word for included within the hit

parts.note: to pip is to hit with a shot
R is short for rex, Latin for king
inc. is the abbreviation for included or inclusive

explanation.surface: The assassin of the archduke and a king are among those hit by the gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Included in' looks like a single container signal, but 'included' supplies letters and only 'in' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo in 1914, the spark of the First World War.

clue.text: Architectural historian against knight being embraced by nobleman

indicators.note: being embraced by means held inside another's arms, so these letters sit inside the nobleman

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
vs is short for versus, meaning against
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An architectural historian opposes a knight being hugged by a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight gives N rather than K because K is taken by the king in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Nikolaus Pevsner was the art and architecture scholar behind the Buildings of England county guides.

clue.text: Appears to be heartless, withdrawing toast

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the word runs backwards
heartless means with the heart cut out, so a central letter goes

parts.note: if something looks big, it appears to be big

explanation.surface: Someone who seems cold-hearted backs out of a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOKS loses its middle O to give LOKS, which reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Skol is a Scandinavian drinking salutation, said when raising glasses, like cheers.

clue.text: Make light, short journey with overnight bag across India

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the bag goes round the India letter
short means cut off, so the last letter of the journey word goes

parts.note: a trip is a journey
a valise is a small travelling case
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Packing light for a short trip across India with only an overnight bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light' sounds like packing light, but it means treat as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: To trivialise something is to treat it as unimportant, making light of it.

clue.text: Forest often flooded, first floating around Georgia

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first words surround the state abbreviation

parts.note: an IPO, initial public offering, is a company's first floating on the stock market
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A flooded forest where something is first seen floating around Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First floating' sounds like debris in water, but it is a business term: a stock market flotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Igapó is Amazonian blackwater forest that stands seasonally inundated by rising rivers.

clue.text: Fine goodness that makes sherry taste nutty

parts.note: f is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
'Lor!' is a dated exclamation, as in 'Goodness!'

explanation.surface: A fine goodness that gives sherry its nutty taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' looks like a quality, but it is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Flor is the yeast film forming on fino sherry in the cask, giving its distinctive nutty tang.

clue.text: Incongruously raw and Lionel Blairesque?

indicators.note: incongruously means out of place, so the letters are set in an unfitting order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Is something raw and odd in the style of Lionel Blair, the British TV dancer and entertainer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lionel Blairesque' reads as one name; Lionel is fodder and Blair points to Eric Blair, George Orwell's real name.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, so writing in his manner can be called Blairesque.

clue.text: Crossbeam's reduced range of movement

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: travel is the range of motion of a mechanical part, such as a piston's travel

explanation.surface: A beam that has a limited range of movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trave is an architectural term for a crossbeam or a bay formed by such beams.

clue.text: Climate protesters about to fret old lady and everyone in France with very dry skin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the protest group's letters go round the next word

parts.note: XR is Extinction Rebellion, the climate campaign group
to fret is to wear away gradually
one's old lady is one's mother, ma
tous is French for everyone

explanation.surface: Climate protesters fret about an old lady and everyone in France suffering parched skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' looks like worry, but its older sense is to wear away. Extinction Rebellion is a UK-founded climate protest group.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeroderma is abnormal dryness of the skin, so a xerodermatous person has very dry skin.
